data.body:
**Landed. Gerrit 2679 merged as `d6669496cae4`, now the tip of `origin/main`** (double-green: `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`, submitted by the operator). Change: `pct_of_cap` no longer clamps; five metrics, five tests, one runbook paragraph.

## AC verdicts

**AC1 — the helper no longer clamps: MET.** `infra/scripts/observability.sh` now reads

    pct_of_cap() {
      printf '%s\n' "$(( $1 * 100 / $2 ))"
    }

Proven by `tests/scripts/test_observability_pct_of_cap_b380.py`, which drives the SHIPPED function definition (lifted out by text — the script is a straight-line probe that cannot be sourced). Over-cap at the live numbers returns 109; exactly at the cap returns 100, so no off-by-one was introduced. RED first on the pre-fix tree with `assert 100 == 109`.

**AC2 — every call site publishes unclamped, and a re-introduced clamp is caught: MET, over FIVE sites not three.** The ticket named three; the follow-up comment added the container writable layer as a fourth; `var_tmp_used_percent` (§2h, story `2ba3`) is the fifth and nobody had counted it. All five are covered by construction because the fix is in the shared helper. Each has an end-to-end over-cap test asserting its true ratio — docker 300, buildkit 240, journal 200, var_tmp 225, container 300 — and each was RED first with `assert 100 == <that value>`.

The "future re-introduction at any single site is caught" half is proven by seeding, not asserted. Re-introducing a clamp at ONE call site only (wrapping the BuildKit `--value` expression, leaving the shared helper honest) turned `test_a_budget_overrun_publishes_its_true_ratio` RED with **`assert 100 == 240`**. In the SAME run `test_storage_and_buildkit_are_published_against_their_own_caps` — an at-cap input expecting exactly 100 — **passed with the clamp seeded**. That contrast is the point: only an over-cap assertion can discriminate, and a proof built on under-cap inputs would have been vacuous, which would be a poor way to verify the fix for a vacuous-check bug. Seed reverted; `git diff` confirmed only the intended change remained. A `2 GiB + 1` case pins the floor-division boundary so a future clamp cannot hide behind it.

**AC3 — checked against every consumer, with an explicit statement: MET. No alarm threshold and no unit needs changing.** All five percentages feed exactly one alarm each, all in `monitoring_autodeploy.tf`: `rebar-docker-storage-cap-high` (407), `rebar-docker-buildkit-cache-high` (446), `rebar-journal-usage-high` (562), `rebar-var-tmp-usage-high` (655), `rebar-container-writable-usage-high` (750). Every one is `GreaterThanThreshold`, `threshold = 85`, `statistic = "Maximum"`, `treat_missing_data = "breaching"`, 300/3/2. **A datapoint clamped to 100 already breached 85**, so every datapoint that fired before still fires — unclamping cannot make an alarm stop firing, it only widens what the alarm can tell apart. No alarm on these five uses `LessThanThreshold`, a band, an upper bound, anomaly detection or metric math; the `LessThanThreshold`/`threshold = 1` alarms in that file (342, 609, 702, 798) watch the 1/0 heartbeats, none of which touch `pct_of_cap`. `monitoring.tf` references only `disk_used_percent` / `root_disk_used_percent`, published by paths that never call the helper. **There are no `aws_cloudwatch_dashboard` resources in the repo at all** — so "a datapoint of 300 rescales every dashboard that shares the axis", the original clamp's stated justification, had no consumer to protect. CloudWatch's `Percent` unit is a label on a double, not a validated range, so 109 and 300 are accepted datapoints and `--unit Percent` stays. No `.tf` file was modified and no `terraform apply` was run. `tests/unit/test_alarm_actions_terraform.py` passes unchanged. `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md` gained a paragraph telling an operator a reading above 100 is real and how far past the cap it means, and the BuildKit alarm row now reads "at, or PAST, its own cap".

**AC4 — re-measure the live overshoot: `[non-codebase]`, satisfied by substitute.** The live condition this criterion asks to re-measure **no longer exists**: the operator pruned that build cache at approximately 10:55 UTC on 2026-09-05 while relieving disk pressure, unrelated to this fix. The BuildKit cache reads 0 now, so the 5.875 GB against a 5.00 GiB budget cannot be re-measured by anyone, and this agent is in any case barred from mutating the production host.

The criterion is tagged `[non-codebase]` because its evidence is a **live host measurement**, which is inherently outside the repository snapshot a completion verifier reads — not because the codebase merely fails to show it. The substitute is arguably stronger than what AC4 asked for: `pct_of_cap 5875000000 5368709120` -> **109**, asserted in `test_a_cap_overrun_publishes_the_true_ratio_not_a_ceiling` at the exact bytes measured live on 2026-09-05. It is reproducible on every CI run, where the host state is gone for good. The ratio the metric now publishes IS `docker system df` divided by `builder.gc.maxUsedSpace`, computed by the shipped function on the recorded inputs.

Someone with host access should confirm on the next natural overshoot; nothing blocks on it, and the arithmetic is pinned either way.

**AC5 — portability: MET.** Pure shell arithmetic; the tests are local pytest driving `bash` over PATH stubs, with no AWS, Docker, systemd or CI-provider trigger. The `[non-codebase]` criterion above is the only one whose evidence is not reproducible from the repository.

## Verification run

81 tests pass across the five observability files plus `test_alarm_actions_terraform.py`, re-run after rebasing onto current `main`. `make lint` green. `make verify` ran on the pre-rebase tree and reported 29 failures — **26 of them `GateCongestedError: gate admission refused: all 4 concurrent slots`**, a shared host-level admission semaphore saturated by other work on the box, with **zero failures in any file this change touches**; re-run serially, 20 of 21 passed and the last failed with a different error that passes when its file runs alone (cross-test contamination). CI's `Verified +1` on 2679 is the authoritative signal and it is green.

## Scope note preserved

This is NOT `regretful-enormous-horsefly` (`docker_unaccounted_bytes` differencing allocated blocks against apparent size). That one produces a wrong NUMBER from sound plumbing; this produced a CENSORED number from a deliberate clamp. The `clamped at 0` lower bound on `docker_unaccounted_bytes` at `observability.sh:259` is a different metric with different semantics and was deliberately left alone.
